reason: Checked the packet marks plus web research on the macro backdrop and on MO. Q4 commentary (geopolitical conflict, high oil, elevated bond yields) favours defensive staples/healthcare dividend payers and an energy hedge, which is exactly the book's tilt; CVX (+11%) is the hedge working. The laggards are MO (-7.8%, about 8% under its fill versus a 20% stop; weak trend on falling cigarette volumes and dividend-durability worries, but earnings are not until 2026-10-29 and the yield and valuation of roughly 14x P/E give some cushion) and NOBL (-4.1%, far from its 15% stop). No stop is near, no leg is closed, and I found no new thesis-breaking news on JNJ, KO, PG or ABBV. Lagging SPY (+3.8%) is a style effect of the defensive mandate, not a signal to abandon it. Any replacement trade would cost 2bps per side plus spread and would mostly swap one dividend payer for another, so holding beats churning.
